fields.features_heading: What Emergent Builds Into Your Friendship Quiz
fields.features_subheading: Emergent builds the questions, scoring, results, and a table of every answer from one prompt. Change any part by asking.
fields.feature_1:
Your answers set the key

Write 10 questions about yourself and answer each one first, such as your usual coffee order. Friends answer from one link, and every guess is scored against yours when they finish.
fields.feature_2:
Friend types instead of a score

Switch to a matching quiz where every option points to a friend type, such as Planner or Listener. The result screen names the type the answers lean toward and says why.
fields.feature_3:
A leaderboard for the whole group

The leaderboard ranks every friend who played by score, with the top guesser first. Keep it hidden until the party and open it when everyone is in the room for the reveal.
fields.feature_4:
Every play saved as a row

Each finished quiz is a row in a database you own, with the player's first name, every pick, and the score or result. Sort by score, or filter by result before the next round.
fields.feature_5:
One question per screen on a phone

Friends tap through one question per screen with a progress bar, which suits a link dropped into a group chat. Emergent puts no cap on how many friends can take the quiz.
fields.feature_6:
Your link, and code you can keep

Publish the quiz on a custom domain, included with Emergent and paid in credits. On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository and run the quiz again next year.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Friendship Quizzes and Who Runs Them
fields.tab_content_1:
Who knows Marisol best, by score

Marisol Ortega wrote a 10-question quiz about herself for her birthday party and answered each question first. Six friends played from one link the week before. The leaderboard put Dev Patel first with 9 of 10 and Rafe Collins last with 4 of 10, and every pick sits in her table for the toast.
fields.tab_content_2:
132 Adventurers headed for one kayak trip

Every incoming first-year at Halden College gets the friendship quiz in August, before move-in, and each friend type maps to a welcome-week meetup. This year 132 students landed on Adventurer and were signed up for the Saturday kayak trip. Their RA, Noor Abbasi, got the list of names by email.
fields.tab_content_3:
Three episodes picked for every Steady Friend

Grace Liu took the friendship quiz on The Porchlight Hour's site after a guest episode. Her answers leaned Steady Friend, and the result page listed the 3 episodes the hosts picked for that type. She left her email, and the app added her to the Steady Friend segment of the show's newsletter tool through its API.
fields.tab_content_4:
The class tally comes back without a name

Ms. Alvarez opens her middle school advisory with the friendship quiz on a Monday, and the app saves the answers with no names attached. All 26 students finished. The tally showed Listener 9, Adventurer 7, Planner 5, and Steady Friend 5, so the next session practiced making a plan with a friend.

fields.howto_title: How to Make a Friendship Quiz
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to make a friendship quiz with fair questions and results worth sharing, then build it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Ask about things friends have seen
fields.howto_step_1_des: Decide whether friends guess facts about you or the quiz names a friend type. A best friend challenge needs your own answers saved as the key. A friend type quiz needs every option mapped to a result. The format shapes every question you write.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Write questions a close friend could answer from time spent together: your usual order at the diner, the song you always skip, the first thing you do on a free Saturday. Leave out facts only family would know, such as a middle name.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Give each question four options of the same kind and about the same length. One long, detailed option next to three short ones stands out, and the score then rewards spotting the odd one instead of knowing you.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Hold the quiz to 8 to 10 questions with one question per screen. That is short enough to finish on a phone between texts. Put the hardest question last, where it can separate two close scores on the leaderboard.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Describe what the answers lean toward, not a verdict on the person: your answers lean toward making the plans and booking the table. Add one thing to try with a friend this week, and keep every result kind enough to post in a group chat.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Choose what lands in the table: a first name, every pick, the score or result, and the time. Ask for an email only if you will send something back, such as a recap of the results. Put that list in your prompt, and Emergent builds the table to match.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Run through the quiz four times, once aiming at each friend type, and make sure every type can come out on top. For a challenge, play as two friends with different scores and check the leaderboard order before the link goes out.

faq_plan.q: What is the best friendship quiz app?
faq_plan.ref: What is the best friendship quiz app?

prov.original: What is the best friendship quiz app?

faq_plan.a: The best friendship quiz app is the one built for the game your group wants. For a best friend challenge, choose one where you write your own answers before anyone plays and friends are ranked on a leaderboard. To learn your own friend type, play the free quiz on this page, which asks for no sign-up.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a friendship quiz?
faq_plan.a: Pick a format, then describe the quiz in a prompt: the questions, your answers or the friend types, and what each play saves. Emergent's AI survey builder writes the quiz and the database behind it. Publish it and send one link to your friends.

faq_plan.q: What is a true best friend quiz?
faq_plan.ref: What is a true best friend quiz?

prov.original: What is a true best friend quiz?

faq_plan.a: A true best friend quiz checks how well a friend knows you. You answer questions about yourself first, such as your comfort food, and your friend tries to pick the same answers. Every correct answer adds to their score. A 10-question quiz gives a score out of 10.

faq_plan.q: Can a best friend friendship quiz show a friend type instead of a score?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Map every option to a friend type instead of scoring guesses, and the result shows which type the picks favor, the same way a style quiz names a style. The quiz on this page works that way, with four friend types and eight questions.

faq_plan.q: What are good friendship quiz questions and answers to start with?
faq_plan.a: Start with everyday picks a friend has seen firsthand. Ask what you order at a coffee shop, with oat latte, black coffee, chai, and hot chocolate as the options. Ask which chore you put off longest, or where you would go on a free weekend. Your own pick becomes the right answer.

faq_plan.q: How do you score a best friendship challenge quiz fairly?
faq_plan.a: Give one point for each answer that matches yours and nothing for near misses. Every player is then judged the same way. For ties, add one last question with a number answer, such as how many houseplants you own, and the closest guess wins. On Emergent, every pick is saved in a database you own, ready to rescore if you change a key answer.

faq_plan.q: Can a friendship quiz maker show results to the whole group?
faq_plan.a: Yes, when it keeps every answer: then it can show a leaderboard or a tally of how the group answered each question. For a quick group vote, such as where to eat, poll questions are faster than a quiz. Emergent puts no cap on responses. A whole class or club can play from the same link.

faq_plan.q: How do you write a toxic friendship quiz that stays respectful?
faq_plan.a: Ask about specific behaviors instead of labels: how often plans get canceled at the last minute, or whether favors go both ways. Write each result as a pattern the answers point to, never a verdict on a real person. In a quiz for students, name a trusted adult they can talk to.

faq_plan.q: What should a true friendship quiz show at the end?
faq_plan.a: Show the score, then each question with the player's pick beside your real answer. Read the misses out loud at the party, since the wrong guesses make the better stories. Keep that reveal on the result screen for the player, and save the full breakdown to your table.

faq_plan.q: Can a friendship quiz work in a classroom?
faq_plan.a: Yes, as a friend type quiz with no names saved. Students answer one question per screen, and the teacher sees a tally of the types to plan a discussion. For graded practice, a vocabulary quiz scores each student instead. Emergent builds either one from a prompt.

quiz.title: Friendship Quiz: What Kind of Friend Are You?
quiz.intro: Eight questions about how you show up for the people you care about. Your result names the friend type your answers lean toward, with one thing to try next.

questions.text: A friend texts that they had a rough day. What do you do first?

options.text: Call them and let them talk it through
Suggest a drive somewhere new to clear their head
Bring takeout to their place like any other Tuesday
Set up a dinner with the group for Friday

questions.text: The group chat goes quiet for two weeks. What happens next?

options.text: You post three dates and ask who is free
You keep sending the usual memes and check-ins
You pitch a last-minute road trip
You message one friend to ask how they are really doing

questions.text: Which plan sounds best for a Saturday with friends?

options.text: A hike on a trail none of you have tried
A long lunch with one friend and no phones
A booked table and a game night after
The same diner you have gone to for years

questions.text: What do friends count on you for most?

options.text: Remembering the details they told you months ago
Getting everyone in the same place
Showing up, every time, without being asked twice
Talking them into something they end up loving

questions.text: A friend moves to another city. How do you stay close?

options.text: A standing video call on the same night each week
A visit within the first month to explore their new city
A shared calendar with the next three visits on it
Long voice notes back and forth

questions.text: What gift are you most likely to give a friend?

options.text: Tickets to something you can do together
A book they mentioned wanting, once, last spring
A refill of the coffee they always drink
A surprise party you organized down to the playlist

questions.text: Which role do you take on a group trip?

options.text: The one who books the rooms and splits the costs
The one who finds the spot not in any guidebook
The one roommates talk to late at night
The one who keeps the trip running the same way each year

questions.text: What makes a friendship feel strong to you?

options.text: Years of small, regular check-ins
Conversations where you both say what you mean
Trying new things side by side
Plans on the calendar that actually happen

results.title: The Planner
results.description: Your answers lean toward making plans happen: you pick the date, book the table, and get the group in one room. Try handing one plan to a friend this month and let them run it and enjoy being a guest for once.

results.title: The Listener
results.description: Your answers lean toward one-on-one time and remembering what friends tell you. You hold on to the small details, like the name of a coworker they mentioned once. Try a walk or a long lunch with one friend this week, with phones put away.

results.title: The Adventurer
results.description: Your answers lean toward new places and last-minute ideas that turn into stories. Try pairing one big idea with a friend who likes to plan, and pick a date before the idea fades.

results.title: The Steady Friend
results.description: Your answers lean toward showing up week after week: the same diner, the regular call, the text that always comes. Try inviting one newer friend into a ritual you already keep.
